To find the stationary points of an equation y = f(x), first find the derivative of the function, f'(x). Then, set the derivative equal to zero and solve for x. The solutions to this equation are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To determine whether each stationary point is a maximum, minimum, or saddle point, you can use the second derivative test. Find the second derivative of the function, f''(x), and evaluate it at each stationary point. If f''(x) is positive, the stationary point is a local minimum. If f''(x) is negative, the stationary point is a local maximum. If f''(x) is zero, the test is inconclusive.
